title: Tracing a Loop
subject: Computer Science
objectives: Students will be able to trace a for loop over range() and record each variable after every pass.
Students will be able to use n % 2 to tell even numbers from odd ones in a loop.
targets: I can trace a loop pass by pass.
I can use % 2 to pick out even or odd numbers.
materials: A projector with a Python shell, to check traces after the worksheet

vocabulary.meaning: Run the code by hand, writing down each variable's value as it changes.
The numbers from a up to b, not including b.

sequence.teacher: Students predict on whiteboards before anyone runs it.
sequence.students: Write a prediction, then show it.

slides.title: Warm-up: predict it
slides.text:
x = 3
x = x + 2
x = x * 2
print(x)
slides.focus: What prints? Write each value of x as it changes.
slides.say: Answer: 10. Ask a student to say each value of x out loud: 3, 5, 10. That's tracing.

sequence.teacher: Model a trace pass by pass on real code, then add an if inside the loop.
sequence.students: Copy the trace table and predict each row before it appears.

slides.say: Spend the most time on range: the stop number is never included.

slides.title: A loop to trace
slides.text:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 4):
    total = total + n
print(total)
slides.focus: How many times does the loop run? What is n each time?
slides.say: Three passes: n is 1, 2, 3. Point out that 4 is the stop and never happens.

slides.title: Trace it pass by pass
slides.problem:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 4):
    total = total + n
print(total)
slides.say: Before each step, ask: what is n now? What was total before this pass?

slides.title: Even or odd?
slides.callout: An if inside the loop runs its check on every pass.
slides.say: Have students say the remainder for 7, 8, and 9 out loud.

sequence.teacher: Trace a loop with an if/else together (we do), then check range on whiteboards.

slides.title: We do: a loop with an if
steps: n = 1: 1 > 1 is False, so the else runs: count = 0 - 1 = **-1**
slides.say: Students write each row on whiteboards before you reveal it: n, which branch runs, and count after the pass.

slides.title: Check: range
slides.prompt: Which values does n take in for n in range(2, 6)?
slides.why: range stops before its second number, so 6 never happens.
slides.say: A is the most common mistake: it includes the stop.

sequence.then: Done? Change Program A so it adds the odd numbers instead, and trace it.
sequence.teacher: No computers until the go-over: the point is tracing by hand. Collect every sheet when time's up.
sequence.students: Trace Program A, then fix Program B.

sequence.teacher: Collect the worksheets, then go over the trace for Program A and run it in the shell to confirm.
sequence.students: Say what they got for each pass before it's shown.

sequence.teacher: Students answer on sticky notes, on their own.

slides.title: Exit ticket
slides.prompt: How many times does for n in range(3, 9): run?
slides.say: Answers of 7 mean the stop is still being counted: start tomorrow there.

checks: What is n on the last pass of range(1, 5)?
What was total before this pass?
What is 9 % 2, and what does it tell you?

misconceptions.response: Write out the values and count them: 4 passes, the stop is never reached.

misconceptions.misconception: total = total + n replaces total with n.
misconceptions.response: Trace one pass on the board: the right side uses the old total first.

support: Give a trace table with the n column filled in.
Let students run one line at a time in the shell after tracing.
extension: Rewrite Program B with range(1, 10, 2) and no if.
Predict what Program A prints if lines 5-6 (the else and its line) are deleted. (It prints 6.)
language: Let students explain a trace by pointing at the table instead of in writing.

walkthrough.think: On pass 1, is n even? Which line runs?
walkthrough.idea: Each pass checks n, then changes total: odd subtracts 1, even adds n.
steps: n = 3 is odd: total = 1 - 1 = 0. n = 4 is even: 0 + 4 = 4.
mistakes: Adding n on every pass and ignoring the else.
Starting each pass from 0 instead of the last total.

walkthrough.think: Where does total end up after the last pass?
walkthrough.idea: The print runs once, after the loop: it shows the final total.
walkthrough.model: It prints 4, because total is 4 after the last pass (n = 4 adds 4 to 0).
mistakes: Thinking print runs on every pass.

walkthrough.think: What should n stop before, so 9 is included?
walkthrough.idea: range stops before its second number, and odd numbers leave remainder 1.
steps: To include 9, the stop must be 10 (11 works too: 10 is even, so it's skipped).
mistakes: Writing 9 as the stop, which leaves 9 out.
Writing 0, which picks the even numbers.

walkthrough.think: Which numbers does the fixed program add?
steps: The odd numbers from 1 to 9 are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
mistakes: Picking 45, the sum of every number from 1 to 9.

assessment: A student who has it fills a trace table for a loop with an if/else inside, pass by pass, and can say what range(a, b) produces and which numbers % 2 picks out.
